transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because most days I just feel really low... like I’m stuck at the bottom of a dark hole. Even when I’m around people I know, I can’t seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling.
How long have you been feeling this low?
It’s been about a year and two months now. It started after that fall I had on the HVAC job, when I hurt my back, and then everything just kind of started falling apart after that.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Not really, no. I used to love hiking and painting, and I’d spend time tinkering at the makerspace or getting into a tricky install at work. Now I just kind of stare at the supplies, or I don’t answer when people call. It all feels like too much, or like there’s no point starting.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I get tense sometimes, but I haven’t paid much attention to whether it’s worry exactly. Mostly I just know I don’t feel right.
Have you ever thought about ending your life?

Yes… I have. I’ve had thoughts like maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. And when the pain and the money stuff all piles up, sometimes I catch myself thinking about ending it. It scares me, but the thoughts are there.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that aren't really there?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people don’t see.
Do you find yourself moving more slowly than usual or having trouble getting out of bed in the morning?

Yes. Everything feels slowed down now. Even getting up from the couch and walking to the kitchen takes more effort than it should, and sometimes it takes me a while just to answer a simple question. People have asked me if I’m okay because I’m moving so slow… like I’m underwater.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Yeah… I think so. My eating’s been really off. Some days I just have coffee most of the day because food kind of turns my stomach. Then late at night I’ll pick at whatever’s in the cabinet, but I’m not really hungry and I don’t even taste it much.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are not your own or that someone is controlling your mind?
No… I don’t think so. My thoughts feel like mine, even when they’re not good. I don’t feel like anyone is controlling my mind.
Have you had periods in your life where you felt really low like this before the accident?
Not really like this before. This has been going on about a year and two months, since I fell on that HVAC job and hurt my back. After that, things just kind of started unraveling.
Do you find that your low mood or energy levels change with the seasons?
I don’t think I’ve noticed it changing with the seasons, no. It feels pretty steady… not like it gets better or worse when the weather changes.
Are there any specific situations or events that make you feel even lower than usual?
I don’t know if there’s one specific thing. Most days I just feel like I’m at the bottom of this dark hole. Even if I’m around people I know, that heavy, hopeless feeling doesn’t really let up.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Not really. I used to love hiking, painting, going to the makerspace and tinkering with things… even figuring out a tricky install at work felt good. Now I just kind of stare at my supplies or don’t answer when people call. None of it feels worth starting.
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt this low, or has it been mostly continuous since the accident?
It’s been mostly continuous since the accident. About a year and two months now, since I fell on that HVAC job and hurt my back… after that, everything just kind of started unraveling.
Do you have days where you feel significantly better than others?

Not really. I mean, some days I can get through them a little quieter than others, but I don’t have days where I feel okay. Most days it’s still that same heavy, hopeless feeling, like I’m stuck at the bottom of a dark hole, even if I’m around people.
Have you had any periods of at least two months where you didn't feel this low since the accident?
No. I haven’t had a stretch like that. It’s been going on pretty much the whole time since the fall on the HVAC job, about a year and two months now.
Are there any specific people, places, or things that make you feel even lower than you already do?

It’s not really one specific person or place. It’s more like… most days I already feel like I’m at the bottom of a dark hole. Even if I’m around people I know, that heavy, hopeless feeling doesn’t really lift.
Did you ever feel this low before the accident on the HVAC job?

No, not like this. I mean, I’d had hard days before, sure, but this… this feeling like I’m stuck at the bottom of a dark hole most days, where I can’t shake the heaviness or hopelessness even around people I know—that wasn’t how I felt before.
Have you had more than one distinct period of feeling this low since the accident?
No, it hasn’t really been separate periods. It’s been pretty constant since the fall at the HVAC job—about a year and two months now, since my back got hurt and everything started unraveling.
Have you had any periods where you felt completely back to normal since the accident?
No, I really haven’t. It’s been going on the whole time, about a year and two months now, ever since that fall on the HVAC job messed up my back and everything started falling apart.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent low mood, loss of interest in activities, changes in appetite and sleep, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness, and recurrent thoughts of death have been present for over a year, meeting the criteria for a major depressive disorder. The absence of any mention of manic or hypomanic episodes and the persistent nature of the symptoms point towards a diagnosis of F33.1, Major depressive disorder, recurrent, rather than F33.2 which would imply a current episode without specifying recurrence.
